$$

question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼1-\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{(2n-1)\pi }{2}x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{(2n-1)\pi }{2}\cdot 0)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=0,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(0)=0.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =1-\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{(2n-1)\pi }{2}\cdot 0) \\ 0 & =1-\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}}\cdot 1 \\ -1 & =-\frac{8}{{\pi }^{2}}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{(2n-1)^{2}} & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
